$comment: What each persona IS in the application, keyed by the username realm-template.json gives it. The realm says who the fifteen people are at the provider; this says what a product's seed writes for each of them, so 'tenant-a-admin' means the same rows in every product. tools/render-devkit joins the two into dev/personas.json and refuses a username named in one file and not the other. `user` is whether the application holds a row for the identity at all (AU6: the provider admitting a person and the application knowing them are different facts). `grants` are {tenant, role_class}: tenant is the symbolic label a product maps to its own tenant id, or null for the global scope; role_class is admin, operator or member, and a product maps each onto its own role names (070 RB3). A product without tenants reads only the global grants and ignores the rest.

platform-admin.exercises: A grant that is global rather than inside one tenant. On a tenant host it is no candidate (TH1); on the default entry it is.

tenant-a-operator.exercises: The middle tier inside tenant A: more than a member, less than the administrator, so a product's role set has three rungs to check against.

tenant-a-member.exercises: The ordinary member of tenant A.

tenant-b-admin.exercises: The same administration in a second tenant, so isolation has two sides.

tenant-b-operator.exercises: Tenant B's middle tier, mirroring tenant A's.

tenant-b-member.exercises: The ordinary member of tenant B, so a member in one tenant can be shown reaching nothing in the other.

two-tenant-member.exercises: AU8: one session acts in one tenant, and switching is an act on the session.

single-tenant-member.exercises: The ordinary case, where one grant is active without a choice.

no-application-access.exercises: AU6: the provider admits the identity, the application does not know it, and it is refused and logged out. Under provider_is_source this is the first-login case instead, and the application writes the user.

deactivated-member.exercises: A disabled identity, refused at the provider before any token exists.

unverified-email-member.exercises: An unverified address, refused at the login page and again at the proxy.

no-provider-access.exercises: AU4: an identity this application never granted access, refused by the provider's gate before any token exists.

user-one.exercises: A plain account, for a product with no tenants: a member of the whole product.

user-two.exercises: A second plain account, so a product with no tenants can show one person's data being another's to nobody.
